_comment: The benign twin of phishing_qr_mfa_lure.json, and the reason the QR
signal is graded rather than binary. Everything a naive quishing
detection keys on is present and identical: an unsolicited MFA
re-enrollment pretext, urgency ('before Friday'), a body with no
clickable links, and a PNG attachment whose QR code is the only way
to act on the message. A detection that fires on 'QR code in email'
calls this malicious, and IT stops using QR codes — or, far more
likely, the detection gets muted.
What makes it benign is checkable, not asserted. The sender is
internal and authenticates with SPF, DKIM and DMARC all aligned to
corp.example; the QR resolves to sso.corp.example, which shares an
organizational domain with the sender; and the message names the
helpdesk ticket a recipient can verify independently. The QR signal
grades itself WEAK on exactly that alignment and carries the
legitimate pattern with it, so the destination is the discriminator
rather than the channel.
Note the weak credential_harvest_path signal fires here too (the
enrollment URL contains /mfa). It is supposed to: that signal is
documented as meaningless alone, and a benign fixture that trips it
is what keeps it honest.
